stage: Stage 3 final connected read of the V04/V05 additions
scope_limits: No whole-chapter or whole-book approval. This read evaluates the two inserted figures and connected passages after Stage 2 repairs. Unchanged full-size and 700 px inspection evidence comes from Stage 1.

V04.passage: Pathway and recordings before the image
V04.reader_question: What is physical, and what was measured?
V04.answer: The preceding pathway section defines the integrator, OMNs and ocular plant, then separates shared from private/downstream variability. The recordings section explicitly gives one OMN plus eye movement per session and explains calibration gain. The new figure therefore maps already introduced objects and observations.

V04.reader_question: Does understanding this picture require later mathematics?
V04.answer: No. The intro states the physical/recording/calculation distinction. The lower filter is an orientation to a fitted conversion, whose full derivation comes later; the reader can identify input spikes and predicted position without knowing a transfer function.

V04.reader_question: Are limits needed for the pictured claims visible?
V04.answer: Yes. Proposed source, one-cell pairing, distinct noise entry points and illustrative signals are explicit. Caption and alt do not make population recordings or proven-attractor claims. Each statement explains a visible relation or its status.

V04.reader_question: Does the paragraph connect the figure to what comes next?
V04.answer: Yes. It distinguishes physical source, one-cell observations and later calculated prediction. The next section fits movement to firing; the following section derives the inverse conversion, completing the operation previewed by the diagram. No equation is silently borrowed to justify the picture.

V05.passage: Measurement-noise and filtering sections before the image
V05.reader_question: Are the plotted variables and both processes understood first?
V05.answer: Yes. The chapter defines MSD and lag, shows noise subtraction, defines local log slope, white-noise intensity A and stationary covariance, derives the one-exponential white-input MSD, then derives the Brownian-input MSD through stationary velocity covariance. D, tau and both short/long-lag limits precede the image.

V05.reader_question: Can the reader connect plot labels to the derivations and compare scales correctly?
V05.answer: Yes. The intro explicitly equates one pole with a single exponential response. The caption prints both own-scale normalizations and limits comparison to shapes, identifying guide theory rather than fitted or measured curves. No equality of physical input strengths is needed.

V05.reader_question: Is either plot behavior asserted without support?
V05.answer: No. The spoken functions and slopes reproduce the just-derived functions. The retained sentence restricts the white short-lag slope one to this example, so readers need not assume the paper muscle model has the same initial slope.

V05.passage: Existing paragraph after the image and next circuit section
V05.reader_question: Are qualifications preserved and does the argument continue naturally?
V05.answer: Yes. The next paragraph supplies fast/slow response, motor filtering, feedback, nonzero-static-gain and correlated-peripheral-source qualifications. The next section moves from a possible accumulating command to a proposed memory circuit. The illustration supports that transition without proving a unique biological source.
